title: Affine pro-etale subsite computes the small pro-etale topos
statement:
Let $X$ be any scheme [def-pc-scheme] with its small pro-etale site $X_{\mathrm{proet}}$ and compatible universes and skeletons [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. Let $X_{\mathrm{aff,proet}}$ be the full subsite whose objects are affine weakly etale maps $U\to X$, with standard pro-etale coverings (finite families of affine weakly etale maps satisfying the covering condition of [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]). Restriction along the inclusion induces an equivalence of topoi
$$\operatorname{Sh}(X_{\mathrm{proet}})\simeq\operatorname{Sh}(X_{\mathrm{aff,proet}}).$$

source.place: Tag 098W, label lemma-alternative: restriction from $S_{\mathrm{proetale}}$ to $S_{\mathrm{affine,proetale}$

proof.text: Pullbacks of affine objects remain affine: map the limiting cone through ProEt.forget and Over.forget and apply Mathlib Scheme.isAffine_of_isLimit to the walking-cospan diagram. The full-subcategory inclusion therefore preserves pullbacks. The weakly etale base-change and composition instances are the Mathlib implementations recorded by the cited leaf.

For U in X.ProEt, use U.left.affineCover. Its charts are affine and their open-immersion maps, followed by U.hom, are weakly etale, using the direct Mathlib etale-to-weakly-etale and composition instances. Zariski covers are quasi-compact weakly-etale covers (zariskiPrecoverage_le_propQCPrecoverage), so this family generates a covering sieve contained in coverByImage of the affine inclusion. This proves IsCoverDense without any condition on X.

A covering sieve S on an affine object U contains a covering presieve R, by Precoverage.mem_toGrothendieck_iff_of_isStableUnderComposition for the pro-etale precoverage. Package the underlying scheme family as a quasi-compact weakly-etale cover E. QuasiCompactCover.exists_hom applied to E.forgetQc gives a finite affine refinement A and a morphism a of covers. Each A.f j followed by U.hom defines an affine weakly-etale object. Finiteness and affineness make A.cover quasi-compact (QuasiCompactCover.of_finite), so its presieve belongs to affineWeaklyEtalePrecoverage. The arrow a.h₀ j, with the equation a.w₀ j, defines the map of pro-etale objects through the chosen member of R. Sieve downward closure puts each refined arrow in S. Thus every covering sieve on an affine object has a finite standard affine refinement. This is the finite-affine-refinement condition of the pro-etale covering definition.

Construct the pretopology J as the infimum of Pretopology.finite and the pretopology of the comapped pro-etale precoverage. Its underlying precoverage is definitionally affineWeaklyEtalePrecoverage. Coverage.toGrothendieck_toPrecoverage and Pretopology.toGrothendieck_toCoverage identify its Grothendieck topology with affineWeaklyEtaleTopology. The preserved pullbacks of step 1 identify the matching-family condition for a J-cover with the condition for its image cover. The latter holds for any sheaf on X.ProEt, because the image cover belongs to the pro-etale precoverage. Presieve.isSheaf_pretopology gives continuity. This uses bind composition for finite presieves, rather than the stronger arbitrary-indexed-composition class.

By continuity, affineWeaklyEtaleTopology is bounded above by the topology induced by the inclusion. Conversely, cover-density from step 2 identifies induced covering sieves with sieves whose pushforward covers. Refine that pushforward by step 3. Fullness and faithfulness lift each factorization back to the affine subcategory, so the original sieve contains a standard finite covering and is covering. This proves equality of the two topologies. The full faithful cover-dense inclusion is consequently an IsDenseSubsite.

Apply the existing Mathlib dense-subsite sheaf-equivalence leaf to the inclusion, with value category Type (max (u+1) v). It has all the required comma-shaped limits since both site object types have universe u+1 and hom types have universe u. The equivalence is the asEquivalence of sheafPushforwardContinuous. Its sheafPushforwardContinuousCompSheafToPresheafIso is exactly the displayed natural isomorphism with restriction. This is the dense-subsite form of Stacks 03A0/098W and uses no enlargement identifying the object and hom universes.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-NH-d9501b3e9 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the item and all six steps in full, together with every cited node's statement (11 nodes plus the fpqc, pro-étale covering, small pro-étale site and weakly étale definitions). The statement matches Stacks 098W (proetale.tex lemma-alternative, l.2696) with the coverings of 098E; Stacks writes S_affine,etale in its display, which is a typo for S_affine,proetale, and the item uses the correct site. Step 1 gives cover-density (03A0(5)): 02GP and etale-implies-weakly-etale plus composition put affine opens in the site, and the family of all affine opens is a covering because each affine open W is itself a member. Step 2 shows that standard coverings are exactly the pro-étale coverings of an affine target, using 01SH as that node states it (098D/098E). Step 3 shows the affine subcategory is a site and the inclusion is continuous: fibre products are taken over an affine U (01I4/01JQ), so no quasi-separatedness of X is used, and the site axioms come from 022D/098C plus weakly-étale stability. Step 4 gives cocontinuity through the finite affine refinement of the affine target, matching clause (1) of the special-cocontinuous definition. Step 5 is correctly marked elementary: local fullness and faithfulness hold for a full inclusion, witnessed by identity coverings. Step 6 applies the 03A0 node, whose statement says the inverse image is precomposition, i.e. restriction; this agrees with the 03A0 proof (g^{-1}G(U)=G(u(U))). Edge cases checked: empty X, the empty covering of an empty affine, non-quasi-compact and non-quasi-separated X, and infinite coverings. There are no new nodes. A search found no pro-étale duplicate; the étale analogue lem-weil-pbc-affine-etale-site-topos is a different site, and the Lean AffineProEt is narrower. tools/review_split.py reports PASS. The eight declared tool_uses are accepted as generic black boxes from chapters that sec-six-functors-basics uses. No SGA is cited, no target was weakened, and there are no changes.
